# Your first release

This tutorial cuts a real release of a small repo using only
`tarsi-serve`. It assumes `tarsi-serve` is on your PATH (see
[Getting started](/getting-started)) and the repo uses conventional
commits.

## 1. Prepare the repo

The repo needs a `tarsi.toml`. The minimal useful one:

```toml
# tarsi.toml
[publish.crates]
enabled = false

[publish.ghreleases]
enabled = false
```

Tag-only releases are the org convention (ADR-0004); without the
`enabled = false` lines both publish targets default to on. Units
default to cargo workspace members — for a non-cargo repo, declare
them explicitly (see [Write a tarsi.toml](/how-to/write-tarsi-toml)).

Make sure the history you want released is conventional:

```bash
git log --oneline
# feat(api): add retries        → minor bump
# fix(core): handle empty body  → patch bump
# chore: tidy imports           → no release on its own
```

## 2. Plan

```bash
tarsi-serve plan --dir .
```

Read the result. Each unit in `plan.units` carries:

* `spec` — resolved unit (name, path, tag format, publish targets)
* `bump` — `major` / `minor` / `patch` / `none`
* `new_version` — the version the bump would write
* `tag` — e.g. `my-unit-v1.2.0`
* `releases` — whether this unit actually releases
* `changelog_markdown` — the rendered changelog section
* `commits` — how many commits were attributed

`plan.unattributed` lists commits that matched no unit's paths —
repo-root files land there. `plan.steps` is the mutation sequence
`release` would run.

Nothing has been written. This is the review gate — always `plan`
before `release`.

## 3. Preview the notes

```bash
tarsi-serve changelog --dir .   # per-unit {unit, version, tag, markdown}
tarsi-serve notes --dir .       # concatenated release notes
```

## 4. Dry-run the release

```bash
tarsi-serve release --dir .
```

`release` is **dry-run by default** — this executes the full plan and
runs every publish target in dry-run mode, reporting what *would*
happen, and writes nothing. Equivalently over ndjson:

```json
{"op":"release","params":{"dir":".","dry_run":true}}
```

## 5. Release for real

Only after the plan looks right and a human approves:

```bash
tarsi-serve release --dir . --yes
```

`--yes` is `dry_run:false`. The mutation phase, in order:

1. Write `CHANGELOG.md` sections per releasing unit (created files
   are tracked for rollback).
2. Bump versions in manifests via `toml_edit` (comments preserved).
3. Stage only the touched files — `CHANGELOG.md`/`Cargo.toml` per unit
   plus root manifests — never `git add -A`.
4. Commit `chore(release): bump versions`.
5. Tag each releasing unit (`{unit}-v{version}`).
6. **Push branch + tags before publishing** — GitHub Releases
   auto-creates tags at remote HEAD otherwise.
7. Run publish targets (crates.io, GitHub Releases) against the
   pushed commit.

The result reports `steps_run`, per-target `publish` reports, and —
on failure — `rolled_back` or a manual-cleanup note for partial
publishes.

## 6. Verify

```bash
git tag -l '*-v*' | tail
git log --oneline -3
tarsi-serve plan --dir .   # now: nothing to release
```

The latest-tag-per-unit range means a second `plan` finds no new
commits since the tags you just pushed.

## Next steps

* Layer org conventions with a profile —
  [Author a release profile pack](/how-to/author-release-profile)
* Tune attribution and overrides —
  [Write a tarsi.toml](/how-to/write-tarsi-toml)
* Script it from an agent — [Drive tarsi-serve ops](/how-to/use-serve-ops)

# Write a tarsi.toml

`tarsi.toml` (or `tarsi.yaml`/`tarsi.yml` — YAML wins on ties) is the
repo's release config. It is a plain [`tarsi_core::Config`](https://docs.rs)
document — the full schema is in [reference/config](/reference/config);
this page is the practical guide.

## Discovery

`tarsi-config` resolves config through scarab-config discovery:

1. `$TARSI_CONFIG` — explicit file, the whole config (no layering)
2. `./tarsi.{yaml,yml,toml}` in the repo being released
3. `~/.config/tarsi/`

When a [release profile](/how-to/author-release-profile) is active,
loading becomes layered instead of first-match:

```
repo tarsi.*  >  profile tarsi.*  >  ~/.config/tarsi/  >  defaults
```

Objects merge key-wise; repo keys win.

## The minimal file

```toml
[release]
strategy = "conventional"
changelog_path = "CHANGELOG.md"
diff_exclude = ["docs/**", "project/**", "*.md", ".github/**"]

[publish.crates]
enabled = false

[publish.ghreleases]
enabled = false
```

## `[release]` — what gets released

| key | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `units` | cargo workspace members | explicit unit list, or a units spec |
| `tag_format` | `{unit}-v{version}` | tag template; `{unit}`/`{version}` expand |
| `changelog_path` | `CHANGELOG.md` | changelog file spliced per unit |
| `strategy` | `conventional` | release strategy — builtin name or inline rules table |
| `default_bump` | none | fallback bump when inference finds nothing |
| `diff_exclude` | `[]` | path globs stripped from commits before attribution (a commit left with no paths is dropped) |
| `unit_overrides` | `{}` | per-unit overrides, keyed by unit name |
| `sync_refs` | `{rules:[]}` | rewrite pack/doc version refs into the release commit |

### Units

Omit `units` entirely for cargo workspaces — every workspace member
becomes a release unit resolved from its manifest. To declare units
explicitly (non-cargo repos, filtered members), use the `units` spec —
see `tarsi_core::unit::UnitsSpec` for the shape (`Explicit { units }`
with per-unit `name`/`path`/`tag_format`/`publish`/`bump` fields).

### Overrides

```toml
[release.unit_overrides.tarsi-xtask]
skip = true

[release.unit_overrides.my-lib]
bump = "patch"          # force a bump regardless of inference
tag_format = "lib-{version}"
publish = ["crates-io"]  # restrict targets for this unit
```

`skip = true` drops the unit from planning entirely (e.g. a lib that
versions with its parent). Override `bump`/`tag_format`/`publish` merge
onto the resolved spec; per-unit values always beat repo-level defaults.

`diff_exclude` matters more than it looks: docs and config churn would
otherwise attribute commits to units and trigger spurious releases. The
org profile excludes `docs/**`, `project/**`, `*.md`, `.github/**`.
Matching paths are stripped from each commit before attribution; a
commit left with no paths is dropped entirely.

### Release strategy

`strategy` is the release *policy* as data — bump inference and
changelog sectioning (P-030). Name a builtin or write an inline
table; absent means `conventional`:

```toml
strategy = "semantic-release-angular"   # builtin preset
strategy = "keep-a-changelog"            # KaC sections, same bump rules

# …or fully custom:
[release.strategy.bump]
fallback = "patch"
[[release.strategy.bump.rules]]
type = "feat"          # raw type token — "deps"/"i18n" work too
bump = "major"

[release.strategy.changelog]
[[release.strategy.changelog.sections]]
key = "features"
heading = "Features"
[[release.strategy.changelog.sections.rules]]
type = "feat"
```

Bump rules fold **max-match** (highest `bump` wins per commit, then
per unit); changelog sections are **first-match** in table order,
which is also render order. `default_bump` fills `strategy.bump.
fallback` when the strategy doesn't set one. Builtins:
`conventional` (default), `semantic-release-angular` (the
commit-analyzer angular preset), and `keep-a-changelog` (the
keepachangelog.com section layout over the conventional bump
rules — `### Added`/`Changed`/`Deprecated`/`Removed`/`Fixed`/
`Security`; full mapping in
[reference/config](/reference/config#keep-a-changelog)). Full schema
in [reference/config](/reference/config#release-strategy); the resolved
strategy echoes on `plan` results as `plan.strategy`.

### Syncing version refs (`sync_refs`)

Repos that ship a tamias pack usually keep `name@version` refs in
docs and the pack manifest's `version:` in lockstep with releases.
`[release.sync_refs]` does that rewrite inside the pipeline — before
the release commit, so refs land in the tagged tree:

```toml
[release.sync_refs]
rules = [
  { files = ["libraries/myco/tamias.yaml"],
    find = "(?m)^version: \"{old}\"",
    replace = "version: \"{new}\"" },
  { files = ["README.md", ".agents/skills/myco/SKILL.md"],
    find = "myco@{old}",
    replace = "myco@{new}" },
]
```

`{old}`/`{new}` are the releasing units' shared old/new version.
Rules skip (with a reported reason) on mixed-version plans, are
idempotent, and show up as `status:"dry-run"` + `changed_files` in a
`bump`/`release` dry-run. Full semantics in
[reference/config](/reference/config#release-sync_refs). With rules
configured, `scripts/release.sh` shrinks to a bare
`tarsi-serve release --dir . --yes`.

## `[publish.*]` — where releases go

Both targets default to **enabled** — set `enabled = false` for
tag-only repos (the org convention).

```toml
[publish.crates]
enabled = true
retry_429 = true        # backoff on crates.io rate limits
max_attempts = 5

[publish.ghreleases]
enabled = true
token_env = "GITHUB_TOKEN"   # env var NAME — never a value
repo = "owner/name"          # optional; defaults to origin remote
assets = ["dist/{unit}-{version}-*"]
```

* `token_env` is a secret **name** resolved via the environment/cuora
  at publish time; values never appear in config or logs.
* `assets` are repo-root-relative globs; `{unit}`/`{version}` expand
  per releasing unit. Magic patterns matching nothing are skipped;
  literal paths must exist.

`[publish] dry_run = true` exists in the schema but the serve surface
already dry-runs `release` by default — prefer `dry_run:false` at the
op level.

## Selecting a profile

```toml
profile = "9aia-release"
```

…or per-invocation, which beats both the config key and
`$TARSI_PROFILE`:

```bash
tarsi-serve plan --dir . --set profile=9aia-release
TARSI_PROFILE=9aia-release tarsi-serve plan --dir .
```

A named-but-missing profile is a hard error — releasing under silent
defaults would surprise.

## Workspace-version caveat

Units whose manifests use `version.workspace = true` share one version
file: the bump is last-writer-wins across releasing units. Keep
workspaces in lockstep or give units explicit versions until per-unit
workspace versions exist (org ledger ADR-0003, decision 4).

# Author a release profile pack

Release profiles are tamias content packs of `type: tarsi` — the org's
conventions (`9aia-release` in `libraries/9aia-release`) ship this way
so every repo can layer them under its own `tarsi.toml`.

## The `type: tarsi` manifest contract

```yaml
# tamias.yaml
name: my-release-profile
version: "0.1.0"
type: tarsi
description: >-
  Human label for the profile — surfaced by the `profiles` op.
```

Payload contract (validated by `tamias-driver-tarsi` at install):

* Payload root MUST carry `tarsi.{yaml,yml,toml}` — a plain
  `tarsi_core::Config` document. **No `[profile]` table**: `profile =
  "…"` is the *selector* key a consumer writes, not something the pack
  carries.
* Extra files may ride along (`styleguide.md`, commit maps, …);
  consumers resolve them relative to the profile dir.
* `description` in `tamias.yaml` is the profile's label; an optional
  top-level `description` in `tarsi.toml` also works for dir-only
  profiles.

## The profile `tarsi.toml`

Keep it to *conventions* — repo-specific overrides belong in the
repo's own `tarsi.toml` (repo keys always win). `9aia-release` is the
reference:

```toml
[release]
strategy = "conventional"   # P-030: builtin name or inline rules table
changelog_path = "CHANGELOG.md"
diff_exclude = ["docs/**", "project/**", "*.md", ".github/**"]
tag_format = "{unit}-v{version}"

[publish.crates]
enabled = false   # org: crates.io is tamias-only (ADR-0004)

[publish.ghreleases]
enabled = false   # org: tag-only releases
```

## How profiles resolve

`tarsi-config` discovery order for a named profile:

1. `--set profile=<name>` on the op (highest)
2. `$TARSI_PROFILE`
3. `profile = "<name>"` in the repo's config

Profile *directories* are found in this order (`find_dir`):

1. `$TARSI_PROFILES_DIR` / `~/.config/tarsi/profiles/<name>/` —
   unversioned dir profiles (dev/pinned)
2. The tamias store — every `<store>/name@label/` carrying a `tarsi.*`,
   newest version label wins (the store commit *is* the placement —
   the driver validates, it does not copy)

Layering with a profile active:

```
repo tarsi.*  >  profile tarsi.*  >  ~/.config/tarsi/  >  defaults
```

## Ship it

`tamias-driver-tarsi` (`crates/tarsi-driver`) is the content driver.
`cargo xtask pack` stages a release build into
`libraries/<pack>/drivers/bin/<triple>/`, and tamias registers
bundled drivers *before* dispatching install — so:

```bash
cargo xtask pack
tamias install --allow-drivers ./libraries/my-release-profile
```

self-provisions the driver and lands the profile in the store,
versioned by label. Verify resolution:

```bash
tarsi-serve profiles                       # lists installed profiles
tarsi-serve plan --dir . --set profile=my-release-profile
```

The driver's `status` verb reports which dir `find_dir` picks for a
name and from which source; `uninstall` removes `profilesDir` copies
(the store entry itself is dropped by tamias).

## Gotchas

* **Dir profiles shadow store versions.** `~/.config/tarsi/profiles/`
  is searched first and carries no version — a stale copy there wins
  over every store version, including ones `tamias remove` dropped.
  The driver only writes there when `profilesDir` is configured
  (opt-in escape hatch).
* **Unsafe names rejected.** Profile names are validated
  (`safe_name`) — stick to lowercase slug names like `9aia-release`.
* **No silent fallback.** Naming a missing profile errors the op;
  there is no "profile not found → defaults" path.

url: /tarsi/how-to/use-serve-ops.md
---
# Drive tarsi-serve ops

Every tarsi surface is an op on `tarsi-serve` — no CLI verbs, no
`--json` flag. This page covers both transports.

## One-shot mode

```bash
tarsi-serve <op> --dir <repo> [--set key=value]… [--yes|--dry-run]
```

`hypha-serve-cli` parses args into the op's `params`, dispatches, and
prints the result JSON. Exit 0 on `ok:true`, 1 otherwise.

```bash
tarsi-serve manifest
tarsi-serve profiles
tarsi-serve plan --dir .
tarsi-serve plan --dir . --set profile=9aia-release --set range=HEAD~5..HEAD
tarsi-serve release --dir . --yes        # the only mutating call
```

Flag mapping:

* `--set k=v` → `params[k] = "v"` (strings; repeat for multiple)
* `--yes` → `params.dry_run = false`
* `--dry-run` → `params.dry_run = true` (the default anyway)

## ndjson service mode

```bash
tarsi-serve    # no args — loop on stdio
```

One request per line, one response per line:

```json
{"op":"manifest","params":{}}
{"ok":true,"result":{"name":"tarsi-serve","version":"0.1.0","ops":[…]}}

{"op":"release","params":{"dir":".","dry_run":true}}
{"ok":true,"result":{"dry_run":true,"plan":{…},"publish":[…]}}
```

Errors come back as `{"ok":false,"error":"…"}` — including release
failures, which also carry the partial `result` (plan, steps run,
rollback report) for inspection.

This is the wire peregrin campaigns and agents use; `tarsi-serve` is
a composition root only — orchestration and UI live in the callers.

## Params reference

Common params (all ops accept `dir`, default `.`):

| param | type | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | string | repo being released |
| `profile` | string | `type: tarsi` profile name (beats `$TARSI_PROFILE` and config `profile`) |
| `range` | string | explicit rev range e.g. `"HEAD~5..HEAD"` — overrides since-last-tag for **every** unit |
| `dry_run` | bool | `release` only; **default `true`** — mutation needs `false` |

## The safe sequence

```text
manifest → profiles → plan → changelog → notes → release(dry_run:true) → release(dry_run:false)
```

Rules of thumb:

* **Always `plan` before `release`.** The plan is the review gate.
* **`dry_run:false` is the `--yes` equivalent** — get explicit human
  or campaign approval first; never run it against a repo you haven't
  planned.
* **`range` is a debugging tool**, not a release mechanism — it
  applies one range to all units and bypasses per-unit tag ranges.
* On failure, read `rolled_back` (clean undo) vs the manual-cleanup
  note (a publish target succeeded before another failed — the tag
  stays, live releases must not be orphaned).

## Calling from code

`tarsi-serve` is a lib too: `tarsi_serve::dispatch(&GitVcs, &Request)`
takes an injected `lasius_vcs::Vcs`, which is how
`tarsi-testkit`'s conformance suite exercises the ops against fixture
repos without a process.

---
url: /tarsi/explanation/release-semantics.md
---
# Release semantics

The semantics below are load-bearing — they are pinned by
**ADR-0003** in the org ledger (`9aia/project`,
`project/adrs/0003-tarsi-release-semantics-plan-dry-run-bump-tag-manifest.md`).
This page is the readable summary; the ADR is the contract.

## Dry-run is the default

`tarsi-serve release` mutates only with `dry_run: false` — the
`--yes` equivalent. Orchestration callers (peregrin campaigns,
agents) opt in explicitly; anything probing a repo gets plans,
never writes. This mirrors the org rule that service surfaces never
mutate unless asked.

## Bump inference

Conventional commits, attributed to units by path prefix. The
inference itself is a **strategy** (P-030) — data-driven rules in
`tarsi.toml`'s `[release] strategy`, defaulting to `conventional`:

| commit | bump |
| --- | --- |
| `feat` | minor |
| `fix` / `perf` | patch |
| `!` / `BREAKING CHANGE:` | major |
| `chore` / `docs` / `test` / … | none — no release |

Bump rules fold **max-match** (a commit contributes the highest
matching `bump`; the unit folds max across commits) against the
commit's **raw type token** — arbitrary types like `deps` are
nameable. Changelog sectioning is the same mechanism: ordered
`sections[]`, first match wins, table order = render order.
`semantic-release-angular` ships semantic-release's commit-analyzer
angular preset as data; `keep-a-changelog` keeps the same bump rules
but renders the six canonical keepachangelog.com sections
(`### Added`/`Changed`/`Deprecated`/`Removed`/`Fixed`/`Security`) —
KaC is a changelog layout, not a bump policy. Custom tables cover
anything else short of
non-semver versioning or plugin execution (the documented P-030
boundary).

`spec.bump` (unit override or explicit unit spec) wins over
inference; the strategy's `fallback` — filled by
`release.default_bump` when unset — is the repo-wide fallback when
inference finds nothing. Commits with empty path lists match every
unit — conservative attribution. `release.diff_exclude` strips
matching paths before attribution (a commit left with no paths is
dropped).

## Per-unit tags, per-unit ranges

Tag format is `{unit}-v{version}` per unit (`tamias-core-v0.4.2`),
not repo-level `v{semver}`. Each unit's commit range is
`{latest-tag-for-that-unit}..HEAD` — units release independently and
only when their own paths changed. `params.range` overrides with one
range for all units.

## Manifest mutation

Versions are written via `toml_edit` (`tarsi-manifest`) — formatting
and comments survive. Units with `version.workspace = true` bump
`[workspace.package].version` instead: **all releasing units in such
a workspace share one bump** (last-writer-wins today; per-unit
workspace versions are a known limitation).

## Ordering and rollback

The mutation phase is strictly ordered — changelogs → manifests →
scoped `git add` (never `-A`) → `chore(release): bump versions`
commit → per-unit tags → **push branch and tags** → publish. The
push-before-publish order is load-bearing: GitHub Releases
auto-creates `refs/tags/<tag>` at remote HEAD when the tag doesn't
exist yet, which would pin the release to the pre-bump commit.

Failure handling:

* Any mutation failure → rollback undoes exactly what ran (remote
  tags deleted, branch reset, local commit/tags removed, created
  changelog files deleted) and the op reports `rolled_back`.
* Publish failures roll back **only if nothing published** — once a
  target succeeded, deleting the tag would orphan a live release, so
  state is left and the report asks for manual cleanup.

## The LLM boundary

There is deliberately no `tarsi-llm`. Changelog polish composes with
**sepia**: the *caller* (peregrin node, agent) may prompt a sepia
session with the rendered changelog. Conventional-commit output is
the only in-repo path — deterministic by construction (ADR-0003,
decision 6).

## Secrets

Config carries env-var **names** (`token_env`, `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`
via cuora secrets records) — never values. The cuora boundary holds
end to end: names in manifests, values in the secrets broker.

## VCS ownership

Git history, tags, and push go through `lasius-vcs` +
`lasius-vcs-git` (org plan P-019). `tarsi-core` is pure — it sees
only `Commit` values; every VCS call lives in `tarsi-serve` (and
`tarsi-testkit` fixtures). New publish targets are a new
`tarsi-publish-*` crate plus a `PublishTarget` variant; serve
dispatch stays a match arm.

---

---
url: /tarsi/explanation/boundary.md
---
# Boundary with tamias and peregrin

tarsi owns **release semantics** — changelog → bump → tag → publish.
Its neighbors own the layers around it:

| neighbor | owns | tarsi's relation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **tamias** | content distribution — fetch, store, cache, dispense; `type:` content drivers | release *profiles* are `type: tarsi` packs; `tamias-driver-tarsi` validates/installs them; the `tarsi-serve` binary itself ships as a `type: files` pack (`libraries/tarsi`) |
| **peregrin** | orchestration — campaigns, multi-machine workflows | `libraries/release` bundle drives `tarsi-serve release --yes`; campaigns call the same ndjson ops humans and agents use |
| **lasius** | git & workspace expertise — `lasius-vcs` port | all history/tag/push goes through `lasius-vcs` + `lasius-vcs-git`; `tarsi-core` never touches git |
| **sepia** | session lifecycle | optional changelog polish — the caller may prompt a sepia session with rendered notes; no in-repo LLM path |
| **cuora** | secrets broker | `token_env` names resolve through env/cuora; values never enter config, manifests, or logs |
| **scarab** | config/template expertise | `tarsi.toml` discovery/layering is `scarab-config`'s `FileSource`/`LayeredFileSource`; tarsi-config is only the wiring |
| **hypha** | distributed substrate | `hypha-serve-cli` is the shared one-shot arg→params shim every `*-serve` bin uses |

## What tarsi is not

* **Not a CLI.** No `tarsi` binary, no verb tree — the surface is
  ops. (The legacy TypeScript changelog CLI under the README's
  bottom half is pre-rewrite reference only.)
* **Not an orchestrator.** `tarsi-serve` composes ports and answers
  ops; scheduling, approval flows, and UI live in peregrin/pavo.
* **Not a publisher of record for the org.** Org repos release
  tag-only; crates.io publishing is tamias-only and GitHub Releases
  are unused (ADR-0004). The `tarsi-publish-*` crates exist for
  external consumers who opt back in per-repo.
* **Not a registry.** It reads git history and writes tags/manifests;
  it does not host anything.

## The dogfooding loop

`tarsi`'s own `tarsi.toml` configures its release — units resolve
from the cargo workspace, `tarsi-xtask` is skipped, both publish
targets are off. Releasing tarsi itself is plan F of PL-014: a human
or campaign decision, never an agent's.

---

---
url: /tarsi/reference/ops.md
---
# Ops wire surface

`tarsi-serve` speaks ndjson JSON-lines: one `{"op": …, "params": …}`
per line on stdin, one `{"ok": …, "result"|"error"}` per line on
stdout — the same protocol shape as `sepia serve` / `tamias-driver`
verbs. `tarsi-serve manifest` returns this list authoritatively.

> Stage-wise note: granular per-stage ops may land as the surface
> grows. The six ops below are the current stable contract; check
> `manifest` for the live list before scripting against anything
> newer.

## Ops

### `manifest`

No params. Returns the service manifest:

```json
{"name":"tarsi-serve","version":"0.1.0","ops":["manifest","profiles","plan","changelog","notes","release"]}
```

### `profiles`

No params (ignores `dir`). Returns every installed `type: tarsi`
release profile:

```json
{"profiles":[{"name":"9aia-release","version":"0.1.0","description":"…","source":"/path/to/dir"}]}
```

Discovery order: `$TARSI_PROFILES_DIR` / `~/.config/tarsi/profiles/`
(dir profiles) then the tamias store (`name@label`, newest label
wins). See [Author a release profile pack](/how-to/author-release-profile).

### `plan`

Params: `dir?`, `profile?`, `range?`. Pure — computes, writes nothing.

```json
{
  "specs": [ …resolved ReleaseUnitSpec… ],
  "plan": {
    "units": [
      {
        "spec": { … },
        "bump": "minor",
        "new_version": "0.3.0",
        "tag": "my-unit-v0.3.0",
        "releases": true,
        "changelog_markdown": "## [0.3.0] …",
        "commits": 4,
        "publish_targets": [{"target":"crates-io","enabled":false}]
      }
    ],
    "unattributed": [{"sha":"…","subject":"…"}],
    "steps": ["write-changelogs","bump-manifests","commit-bump","tag","push","publish"],
    "strategy": {"name":"conventional","resolved":{…rules…}}
  }
}
```

`strategy` echoes the release strategy resolved from
`[release] strategy` (P-030) — `name` is the builtin name or
`"custom"` for inline tables; `resolved` is the full rule set that
produced the bumps/changelogs.

### `changelog`

Same params as `plan`. Returns only the releasing units' rendered
notes:

```json
{"changelogs":[{"unit":"my-unit","version":"0.3.0","tag":"my-unit-v0.3.0","markdown":"…"}]}
```

### `notes`

Same params. Concatenated `changelog_markdown` of all releasing units
in plan order:

```json
{"notes":"## [0.3.0] …\n## [1.1.0] …\n"}
```

### `release`

Same params plus `dry_run` (**default `true`**). Executes the plan.

Dry-run result:

```json
{"ok":true,"dry_run":true,"plan":{…},"steps_run":[],"publish":[{"target":…,"ok":…,"dry_run":true}…]}
```

Real result (`dry_run:false`):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "dry_run": false,
  "plan": {…},
  "steps_run": ["write-changelogs","bump-manifests","sync-refs","commit-bump","tag","push"],
  "publish": [ {"target":"github-release","ok":true,…} ],
  "sync_refs": {"status":"applied","old":"0.1.0","new":"0.2.0","changes":[…]}
}
```

`sync_refs` reports the `[release.sync_refs]` stage (pack/doc
version-ref rewrites folded into the bump commit — see
[config](/reference/config#release-sync_refs)): `status` is
`disabled` (no rules), `skipped` (+`reason`, e.g. mixed-version
plan), `dry-run`, or `applied`; `changes[]` lists per-rule
file/replacement counts and `changed_files` the touched paths.
Dry-run results carry the same shape with `status:"dry-run"`. The
`"sync-refs"` `steps_run` entry appears only when rules are
configured.

Failure shapes:

* Plan/build error → op-level `{"ok":false,"error":"…"}`.
* Mutation failure → `ok:false` result with `rolled_back` per-step
  report (remote tag deletes, branch reset, local cleanup).
* Publish failure with nothing published → rollback, same shape.
* Publish failure after a success → `ok:false`, `rolled_back:
  {"attempted":false,"reason":"…manual cleanup…"}` — state left in
  place deliberately.

`steps_run` is the mutation-phase ledger; `publish` reports carry
per-target `ok`, `disabled`, and target-specific fields (e.g. gh
release URL, crates.io warnings).

## Common params

| param | type | default | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | string | `"."` | repo root being released |
| `profile` | string | — | profile name; precedence: param > `$TARSI_PROFILE` > config `profile` |
| `range` | string | per-unit tag range | `"a..b"` rev range applied to **every** unit |
| `dry_run` | bool | `true` | `release` only — `false` is the mutation opt-in |

## One-shot mapping

`hypha-serve-cli` translates argv to params:

```bash
tarsi-serve release --dir . --set profile=9aia-release --yes
# ≡ {"op":"release","params":{"dir":".","profile":"9aia-release","dry_run":false}}
```

`--set k=v` values are strings; `--yes`/`--dry-run` set `dry_run`.

---

---
url: /tarsi/reference/config.md
---
# tarsi.toml schema

The config document is `tarsi_core::Config` — TOML or YAML
(`tarsi.yaml`/`tarsi.yml` preferred on discovery ties). Pure serde
types in `crates/tarsi-core/src/config.rs`; loading/layering in
`tarsi-config`. Secret **names** appear (`token_env`); values never
do.

## Top level

```toml
profile = "9aia-release"   # optional — selector, not a table

[release]
…

[publish]
…
```

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `profile` | string | — | named `type: tarsi` profile to layer under this file |
| `release` | table | defaults | release planning config |
| `publish` | table | defaults | publish target config |

## `[release]`

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `units` | spec | cargo workspace members | explicit units (`UnitsSpec::Explicit { units }`) |
| `tag_format` | string | `{unit}-v{version}` | tag template; `{unit}`, `{version}` expand |
| `changelog_path` | string | `CHANGELOG.md` | changelog file spliced per unit |
| `strategy` | string | table | `conventional` | release strategy — builtin name or inline rules table (below) |
| `default_bump` | bump | — | fallback bump when inference finds nothing (folded into the strategy's `fallback`) |
| `diff_exclude` | `[string]` | `[]` | path globs stripped from commits before attribution; a commit left with no paths is dropped |
| `unit_overrides` | table | `{}` | per-unit overrides by unit name |
| `sync_refs` | table | `{rules:[]}` | pack/doc version-ref rewrites before the release commit |
| `styleguide` | string | `keep-a-changelog` | **deprecated** — superseded by `strategy.changelog`; still parsed, ignored |

`bump` values: `"major"` | `"minor"` | `"patch"` | `"none"`.

### `[release] strategy`

The release *policy* as data (P-030): bump inference and changelog
sectioning. Either a builtin name or an inline table — absent means
`conventional`, the pre-strategy behavior.

```toml
strategy = "conventional"            # builtin name, OR inline:

[release.strategy.bump]
fallback = "patch"                   # bump when no rule matches

[[release.strategy.bump.rules]]
type = "feat"                        # raw conventional type token; "*"/absent = any
scope = "core-*"                     # optional: exact or trailing-* glob
breaking = true                      # optional: pin the !/BREAKING CHANGE flag
not_type = ["fix"]                   # optional: type tokens that veto the match
bump = "minor"                       # major|minor|patch|none

[release.strategy.changelog]
[[release.strategy.changelog.sections]]
key = "added"                        # stable section id
heading = "Added"                    # rendered as `### Added`
[[release.strategy.changelog.sections.rules]]
type = "feat"                        # same matcher fields, no `bump`
```

Semantics:

* **Bump rules are max-match** — a commit contributes the highest
  `bump` across its matching rules; a unit folds max across its
  commits (semantic-release commit-analyzer's "highest release
  type wins" — rule order can't be gamed). `fallback` applies when
  inference finds nothing; `release.default_bump` fills it when the
  strategy doesn't set one.
* **Changelog sections are first-match** — a commit lands in the
  first section (table order) with a matching rule; table order is
  also render order. Commits matching nothing are dropped.
* Matchers run on the commit's **raw type token** — `deps`,
  `i18n`, and other non-`CommitKind` types are nameable.
* Each absent `strategy.*` sub-table defaults to the `conventional`
  rules, so `[release.strategy.bump]` alone keeps the conventional
  changelog.
* Builtin names: `conventional` (default — byte-identical to the
  pre-P-030 hardcoded policy), `semantic-release-angular` (the
  commit-analyzer angular preset as data), and `keep-a-changelog`
  (the keepachangelog.com section layout — see below).
* The resolved strategy echoes on `plan` results as
  `plan.strategy {name, resolved}` (`name` = the builtin name or
  `"custom"`).

What can't be data stays code: changelog render formats beyond
section/heading/order, non-semver versioning, non-conventional
commit parsing, anything needing execution (P-030 boundary).

#### `keep-a-changelog`

Keep a Changelog (keepachangelog.com) is a *changelog layout*, not
a bump policy — the builtin keeps `conventional`'s bump rules
verbatim and swaps only the section table for the six canonical
sections, in keepachangelog.com order:

| section | commits |
| --- | --- |
| `### Added` | `feat` |
| `### Changed` | `refactor`, plus breaking commits of types with no section of their own (`chore!`, `deps!`, unknown `!` types) |
| `### Deprecated` | `deprecate`, `deprecation` |
| `### Removed` | `revert`, `remove` |
| `### Fixed` | `fix`, `perf` |
| `### Security` | `security` |

Breaking commits of section-owning types stay in their own
section (`fix!`→Fixed, `security!`→Security, …) — Changed's
catch-all vetoes them via `not_type`. Types outside the table
(`chore`, `docs`, `test`, `deps`, `release`, …) still count for
bump inference but are dropped from the changelog. KaC-named
types (`deprecate`, `revert`, `remove`, `security`) are
changelog-only here — they don't move the version unless
`default_bump` fills the fallback; a repo that wants e.g.
`revert`→patch takes the same table inline with one extra bump
rule.

### `[release.unit_overrides.<name>]`

| key | type | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bump` | bump | force this unit's bump (beats inference) |
| `tag_format` | string | per-unit tag template |
| `publish` | `[target]` | restrict publish targets (`"crates-io"`, `"github-release"`) |
| `skip` | bool | drop the unit from planning entirely |

### `[release.sync_refs]`

Rewrites stale version refs in repo files *inside* the `bump`/`release`
pipeline — after manifests are bumped, before the release commit — so
the tagged tree is self-consistent. This is the stage that replaced the
per-repo `scripts/release.sh` plan+`sed` pre-step (T-039): pack
`tamias.yaml` manifest versions and `name@ver` README/SKILL install
examples.

```toml
[release.sync_refs]
rules = [
  # pack manifest version line (line anchor needs (?m))
  { files = ["libraries/myco/tamias.yaml"],
    find = "(?m)^version: \"{old}\"",
    replace = "version: \"{new}\"" },
  # doc refs — global, like the old `sed s|name@old|name@new|g`
  { files = ["README.md", ".agents/skills/myco/SKILL.md"],
    find = "myco@{old}",
    replace = "myco@{new}" },
]
```

| key | type | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rules` | `[rule]` | rewrite rules applied in order; empty = stage disabled (default) |
| `rule.files` | `[string]` | repo-root-relative globs; non-matching globs are skipped |
| `rule.find` | string | regex matched against file contents — **required** |
| `rule.replace` | string | literal replacement — **required** |

`{old}`/`{new}` expand to the releasing units' shared
`current_version`/`new_version`. Inside `find` they are
regex-escaped (so `.` stays literal); inside `replace` they expand
literally. Patterns are **not** auto-bounded — `app@{old}` matches
the `app@1.2.3` prefix of `app@1.2.30`, exactly like the old `sed`
pre-steps; add `\b` when a boundary is needed (`regex` has no
look-around). Use `(?m)` for line anchors.

Semantics:

* **Single-version only** — sync needs one unambiguous `old → new`
  pair. A plan whose releasing units disagree on `new_version` (or
  `current_version`) reports `status:"skipped"` and the release
  proceeds unsynced — the shims' `len(vs)==1` guard.
* **Idempotent** — rules match the *old* version; once refs say
  `new`, nothing matches and the stage reports zero changes.
* **Dry-run** — `bump`/`release` with `dry_run:true` (the default)
  reports `status:"dry-run"` plus `changed_files` without writing.
* Results surface as `sync_refs{status, reason?, old, new,
  changes[], changed_files?}` on `bump` and `release`; `steps_run`
  gains a `"sync-refs"` entry between `bump-manifests` and
  `commit-bump` when rules are configured. Synced files are staged
  into the release commit itself — no separate pre-commit.

## `[publish]`

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dry_run` | bool | `false` | schema-level flag; the serve op's `dry_run` param is what callers use |

### `[publish.crates]`

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | bool | `true` | crates.io publishing on/off |
| `retry_429` | bool | `true` | backoff on crates.io rate limits |
| `max_attempts` | int | `5` | publish attempts per unit |

### `[publish.ghreleases]`

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | bool | `true` | GitHub Releases on/off |
| `token_env` | string | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | env var **name** holding the token |
| `repo` | string | origin remote | `owner/name` override |
| `assets` | `[string]` | `[]` | repo-root globs; `{unit}`/`{version}` expand per unit |

## Layering

With a profile resolved, config loads through
`LayeredFileSource` — objects merge key-wise, later layers fill gaps:

```
repo tarsi.*  >  profile tarsi.*  >  ~/.config/tarsi/  >  defaults
```

Without a profile, discovery is first-match:
`$TARSI_CONFIG` → `./tarsi.*` → `~/.config/tarsi/`. A missing
profile name is a hard error; a present-but-broken `tarsi.*` file
always errors loudly.

## Example

See `tarsi.toml` at the repo root (dogfooding config) and
`libraries/9aia-release/tarsi.toml` (the org profile).

---

---
url: /tarsi/reference/pack-layout.md
---
# Pack layout

tarsi ships to the org as two tamias packs under `libraries/`.

## `libraries/tarsi` — the command pack

`type: files` — ships the `tarsi-serve` binary. There is no `tarsi`
CLI and no `shim: cli` bin by design (PL-014 surface split:
release-expertise libs + `tarsi-serve` only).

```yaml
# tamias.yaml (abridged)
name: tarsi
version: "0.1.0"
type: files
description: >-
  Generic release tool — changelog → semver bump → tag → publish.
bins:
  - name: tarsi-serve
    payload: tools/bin/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tarsi-serve
```

Layout:

```
libraries/tarsi/
├── tamias.yaml          # the manifest above
└── tools/bin/<triple>/  # gitignored — `cargo xtask pack` stages
    └── tarsi-serve      #   release builds here per host triple
```

```bash
cargo xtask pack                          # build payload
tamias install ./libraries/tarsi          # deploy tarsi-serve → PATH
# or, once published: tamias install tarsi@<ver>
```

Dev shortcut: `cargo xtask install` puts a release `tarsi-serve` in
`~/.local/bin` without the pack flow.

## `libraries/9aia-release` — the org profile pack

`type: tarsi` — the org's release conventions as a layered config
profile (PL-014 D2).

```
libraries/9aia-release/
├── tamias.yaml    # name/version/type: tarsi/description
├── tarsi.toml     # THE profile — a plain Config document
└── drivers/bin/<triple>/   # gitignored — `cargo xtask pack` stages
    └── tamias-driver-tarsi #   the content driver here
```

The `type: tarsi` contract:

* payload root MUST carry `tarsi.{yaml,yml,toml}` — no `[profile]`
  table (`profile` is the consumer-side selector key)
* `tamias.yaml`'s `description` is the profile's human label
* optional extras (`styleguide.md`, commit maps) resolve relative to
  the profile dir

Install self-provisions the driver — tamias registers bundled drivers
before dispatching `install`:

```bash
cargo xtask pack
tamias install --allow-drivers ./libraries/9aia-release
```

The store commit is the placement: the profile resolves by name,
versioned by label, the moment tamias commits it. See
[Author a release profile pack](/how-to/author-release-profile).

## xtask verbs

| command | does |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo xtask check` | fmt + clippy `-D warnings` |
| `cargo xtask test` | whole suite (nextest if present) |
| `cargo xtask pack` | release-build `tarsi-serve` → `libraries/tarsi/tools/bin/<triple>/` **and** `tamias-driver-tarsi` → `libraries/9aia-release/drivers/bin/<triple>/` |
| `cargo xtask install` | release `tarsi-serve` → `~/.local/bin` (dev shortcut) |

Both payload dirs are gitignored build artifacts — the manifests are
the source of truth.

---

---
url: /tarsi/reference/crates.md
---
# Crates

Rust workspace, ports-and-adapters — the same anatomy as
tamias/bupha/peregrin. `tarsi-core` is pure domain (no I/O);
`tarsi-serve` is the composition root and the only shipped binary.

| crate | role |
| --- | --- |
| `tarsi-core` | pure domain — `Config`/`ReleaseConfig`/`PublishConfig` serde model, `plan_release` (bump inference + attribution + changelog render), `Bump`, `Commit`, `PublishTarget`, `ReleaseUnitSpec`/`UnitsSpec`. No I/O. |
| `tarsi-config` | config wiring — scarab-config `FileSource`/`LayeredFileSource` discovery, `$TARSI_CONFIG`, profile resolution (`profile.rs`: dir profiles + tamias-store profiles, `find_dir`/`list_profiles`). |
| `tarsi-manifest` | unit resolution + version writes — cargo-workspace member discovery, `apply_config` overrides, `toml_edit`-based `write_unit_version` (workspace-version aware). |
| `tarsi-publish` | publish port — `Publisher` trait + `PublishJob`; dispatch over target impls. |
| `tarsi-publish-crates` | crates.io publish impl (`publish`/`yank` via cargo, 429 retry). |
| `tarsi-publish-ghreleases` | GitHub Releases impl — release + asset upload, `target_commitish` pinning. |
| `tarsi-publish-dryrun` | dry-run publisher — reports what would publish, touches nothing. |
| `tarsi-driver` | `tamias-driver-tarsi` — the `type: tarsi` content driver (capabilities/install/deploy/uninstall/status/health/logs/hooks); validates profile packs, optional `profilesDir` materialization. |
| `tarsi-serve` | **the binary** — ndjson ops loop + `hypha-serve-cli` one-shot; composes config/manifest/lasius-vcs/publish into the six ops. Lib (`dispatch`/`serve`) + thin `main.rs`. |
| `tarsi-testkit` | golden plan corpus (`golden_cases()`) + serve-op conformance suite (`serve::assert_*`) over `lasius_vcs::Vcs` fixtures. |
| `xtask` | check / test / pack / install |

## Key external deps

* `lasius-vcs` + `lasius-vcs-git` — all git history/tag/push (P-019);
  `tarsi-core` sees only `Commit` values.
* `scarab-config` + `scarab-config-file` — config discovery and
  layering (P-017); no `tarsi-config-*` format crates.
* `hypha-serve-cli` — the shared one-shot argv→params shim.
* `semver`, `toml_edit`, `serde`/`serde_json` — versions, manifest
  mutation, the wire.

API docs: `bun run docs:api` renders `cargo doc` into
`public/api/` (linked from the built site under `/tarsi/api/`).

---

---
url: /tarsi/getting-started.md
---
# Getting started

tarsi is the org's release plane: it turns conventional commits into a
release — changelog → semver bump → tag → publish. There is **no
`tarsi` CLI**; the surface is `tarsi-serve`, an ndjson ops binary with
a one-shot front door (PL-014, org ledger ADR-0003).

## Install `tarsi-serve`

The command ships as a tamias pack (`libraries/tarsi` — `type: files`
declaring `tarsi-serve` as a `tools/bin/<triple>/` payload bin).

```bash
# From a tarsi checkout:
cargo xtask pack    # release-build → libraries/tarsi/tools/bin/<triple>/
tamias install ./libraries/tarsi   # deploys `tarsi-serve` onto PATH
```

Dev shortcut without tamias:

```bash
cargo xtask install   # release `tarsi-serve` → ~/.local/bin
```

## Check the wire

```bash
tarsi-serve manifest
# → {"name":"tarsi-serve","version":"…","ops":["manifest","profiles","plan","changelog","notes","release"]}
```

Two modes:

* **No args** — ndjson JSON-lines loop on stdio: one
  `{"op": …, "params": …}` per line in, one
  `{"ok": …, "result"|"error"}` per line out.
* **`tarsi-serve <op> [--dir D] [--set k=v]… [--yes|--dry-run]`** —
  one-shot via `hypha-serve-cli`; prints the result JSON, exit 0/1.
  `--yes` maps to `dry_run: false`; `--dry-run` forces the default.

## Plan your first release

Inside a repo with a `tarsi.toml` (or none — units default to cargo
workspace members):

```bash
tarsi-serve plan --dir .
```

The result lists each unit in topo order: inferred bump, new version,
tag, rendered changelog markdown, and publish targets — all computed,
nothing written. The full walkthrough is in
[Your first release](/tutorials/first-release).
